title: Substituting, Kid Thomas, and the Rabbit's Foot show
summary: Asked about substituting, he says he would have preferred trumpet, then tells of a Jackson band and joining the Rabbit's Foot Minstrels, doubling on trumpet.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: now did you ever have to substitute on any other instruments like what did you get one set off or a number off now and then so you could go and eat or anything well well no yes what no I had a racket it would cost me a nickel I'd break a straight take two hours to fix it that was the only racket I've heard sometimes like they take turns about to keep the drummer going all the time and one other guy would go and take the drummer's place and he could go out

well Bill I said this I love music and if I had my life to live over again I wouldn't be nothing else but a musician but not a badger player I'd be a trumpet player this time I better be you see cause everybody the bad you see I read in a little book kid Thomas with his enormous power he can play for 14 hours without stopping yeah but he don't play seven notes in them 14 hours either he said ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta-ta Jackson and we had a Jackson Mississippi that wasn't, we had a real good band. But it didn't last too long. We went out on the road for a while. Must have lasted about eight or nine months. And conditions was bad on the road. So when I come back to Jackson, I got a very good friend in Jackson, Joe White. Fine drummer man off the Rabbit Foot Menstrual Show. Him and Manza Campbell supposed to be two of the greatest in the world. So he used to feature this number on the show called OU Drummer. And you never heard nobody play it like him and Manza Campbell. So I went on the show with him and after I played for old man Walcott, he said, well Joe, this man is everything you say he is with a banjo. But no man on my show plays one instrument. He must double on something else. So I had a friend from New Orleans was on the show, Skinny, played tuba. So he told me, say ain't nothing to it, Joe. He said, just get a horn and I'll show you your finger. So and so. Well, I took a peck horn. Well, I didn't like a peck horn. I'm all after. I didn't like that. So I fooled around, went in the back and I got me a trumpet. And I sat down and took my banjo and figured that trumpet out. And I joined that band. I was playing enough trumpet to hold myself up.
